title: Throwing Errors and Sync try/catch Check
description: throw, Error, try/catch/finally, and sync error bubbling.

options.text: `5`, then `caught: Cannot divide by zero`, then `done`
`5`, then `Infinity`, then `after divides`, then `done`
`5`, then `caught: Cannot divide by zero`, then `after divides`, then `done`
Only `caught: Cannot divide by zero` (script crashes before `done`)

questions.explanation: First call prints `5`. The second throws, so `after divides` is skipped; `catch` prints the message, then `done` still runs outside the try.

options.text: `before` then `boom`
`before`, `after throw`, then `boom`
Only `boom`
`before` then `after throw`

questions.explanation: After `throw`, the rest of the `try` block is skipped. Control jumps to `catch`, which prints `err.message`.

questions.prompt: What does `finally` do in a sync `try` / `catch` / `finally`?

options.text: It always runs — after a successful `try` or after `catch`
It runs only when an error was thrown
It runs only when no error was thrown
It replaces `catch` and receives the error

questions.explanation: `finally` is for cleanup that must happen either way — success or failure.

questions.prompt: A function throws and has no local `try` / `catch`. What happens?

options.text: The error bubbles up to the caller (and further, until caught or the script crashes)
JavaScript converts it to `undefined` and continues
Only that function stops; the caller always keeps running normally
It is silently ignored unless you use `async`

questions.explanation: Sync errors propagate up the call stack. Catch at the level that can handle them; uncaught errors typically crash a Node script.

questions.prompt: Why prefer `throw new Error("Expected a string")` over `throw "Expected a string"`?

options.text: `Error` gives `.message` (and a stack); bare strings make `catch` harder to use consistently
Bare strings cannot be thrown in JavaScript
`new Error` is required for `try` / `catch` to work at all
Strings are only for `async` errors

questions.explanation: You can throw other values, but `Error` is the convention so catch blocks can rely on `err.message` and debugging tools.
